reviewMethod: Independent visual sweep of every page of the 2023 deferred Higher Level English question paper (LC020ALP000EV, 44 pages: cover, instructions, Questions 1-10 on pages 3-41 with the answer-space-only pages 13, 16, 20, 25 and 27, extra-work pages 42-43 and the back cover) and its deferred marking scheme (18 pages: cover, the note on deferred schemes on page 2, a title page, solutions for all ten questions on pages 4-16, the blank page 17 and the back cover), each rendered to PNG at 1.5x and read. Every printed ask, mark placement, scale and part total was transcribed against the original layout, and the scheme arithmetic was re-worked line by line, including the matrix product, the Dijkstra and dynamic-programming tables, and the early and late times. The scheme prints a solution and marks for every part of all ten questions, so no task is unpriced. June 2023 Higher (same syllabus and booklet format: answer any eight questions) was the template for task boundaries, credit ladders, topics and wording, with June 2024 and 2025 for scale shapes. The scheme title page is headed "M32C 2024" although its cover reads Leaving Certificate 2023 Deferred Examinations; no mark is affected. No earlier deferred cards exist, so there are no card corrections.
progressIdentityReview: No 2023 deferred Applied Mathematics cards have shipped (no am-2023-hl-deferred- identity in the card source, the compiled reviewed bank or the alias map), so no identity is retained or retired. Suffixes follow June 2023 style; separately priced outputs inside one printed ask use descriptive suffixes (3-i-cd, 3-ii-g6, 3-iii-g6, and 8-i-a with 8-i-b). The deferred card prefix differs from June's am-2023-hl- so these suffixes cannot collide with June 2023 cards.

papers.markingGuideNote: The deferred scheme prints its mark placements and three marking scales but no general marking instructions; its own note says its solutions are not exhaustive and alternatives may be acceptable. These cards apply the general instructions of the June 2023 Higher scheme (same syllabus and format): use the published scale where printed. Other placements allow 2 for a partially correct element. Deduct 3 for a mathematical error, or 1 for a slip or minor misreading; do not deduct an error twice. The Q9(ii) table loses 1 for each incorrect entry. Alternative valid methods are accepted.
papers.boundaryReview: Every step placement is a 5 except Q1(a)(i) (the product AB) and Q2(a)(i) (the weighted graph), each one printed 10. Q2(a)(ii) and Q9(iii) are printed 15 [0/6/9/12] scales and Q6(b) a printed 20 [0/8/14/17] scale; Q2(a)(ii) keeps the time, route and algorithm name together under its scale, and Q9(iii) the early and late times. Q9(ii) is one 10-mark table with −1 for each incorrect part, not thirteen one-mark tasks. Q3(i) gives 5 for forming the second-order equation and 5 for the values of c and d, so two tasks. Q3(ii) and Q3(iii) each give three 5s to the expression for Gₙ and a separate final 5 to G₆, so each is an expression task (15) and a G₆ task (5). Q8(i) prints "5, 5", one 5 for each block's force diagram, so two tasks sharing one crop. Q8(ii) acceleration and tension share the final 5 and stay with the two equations of motion. Q8(v) the extra 0.12 m is a step towards the total displacement. Q10(iii) speed and direction share one 5. Q6(a)(iii) both sketches share one 5. Q7(i) has five 5s, the first on the before-and-after velocity table. Required method steps are not split into separate tasks.

schemeNotes.4-iv: A misprint in the scheme: the first line integrates "dp" with a lower-case p, although the variable is P (read it as dP).
schemeNotes.7-iii: A sign slip in the scheme: it writes F = −kx, then integrates kx rather than −kx. Its answer, W = ½kx², is the work done against the restoring force.
schemeNotes.10-iv: A misprint in the scheme: "sp" in the last line should read "so".
